brief: The river has nothing of the town in it. Thirteen columns of water run down the middle of every wide shot and the only things reflected in them are the MOON's disc and one static linear gradient over rows 3-12, baked into the ground cache and called 'the bank's reflection, smeared toward us'. The bridge stands over the water and is not in it; nor the mill wheel, the moorings, the lamps down both banks, the clock tower, the spire, the far terrace, the willow, the punts. Put the town in its river. The geometry is already written: project() lifts z NORTHWARD, so a NEGATIVE z is the mirror of a positive one - the same solve dialThrow does for a shadow, with the sun replaced by the eye. Reflect the standing things that actually meet the water, fade them with depth and distance from the bank, and let windF break them: the source already describes the boat lantern's reflection as 'chopped into shorter, jittering bars' on a windy night, so that vocabulary exists too. A 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. This is the bet - take the swing.
successLooksLike: At Wide on a still evening the bridge, the clock tower, the church spire and the lit lamps are legible IN the water, so the river reads as a surface the town stands ON rather than a slab beside it - and a windy day chops the same images into bars. WATER's sd/mean moves off 0.151 and the moved pixels are the town's SHAPES, against a same-code control run.
avoid: Do NOT bake it into the ground cache: the light moves through the day and the lamps are lit after applyLight, so this is a live pass on the drawSunShade/drawCloudShade model, and any lit reflection must REGISTER its point and repaint in a screen pass after the multiply, exactly as BARGE_LAMP and PUNT_LAMPS already do. Do NOT add a new water hash - the flatness is the absence of the TOWN, not of texture, and one uniform hash is a texture and never a place. Do not reflect everything: choose what meets the water, and price the pass with frame-cost.mjs in weather at every camera, because perf.mjs will not see it.
